slice: saying of 26 October, phosphorus, sulfur and metals as ghosts

items.text: In the author's saying, phosphorus, sulfur and each metal are ghosts on a periodic table of ghosts, versions of the one atom/carbon, as each element is: DNA's phosphorus and haem's iron then are the one atom/carbon in a phosphorus relation and an iron relation, and the weight of "no other elements" rests wholly on its breaking for versions, still to name, beside this entry's own breaking, which inner X-ray lines and line patterns press strongly.

With phosphorus, sulfur and metals as ghost versions of one atom/carbon in the author's saying, arsenic, phosphorus's neighbour in its group, failing to take phosphorus's place in a living cell's DNA is a record of two versions with relations that do not exchange, and oxygen, nitrogen and hydrogen as three views beside phosphorus, sulfur and metals as other versions asks what parts a view from a version.
